rationale: ROUND 2 of corr 53ae1501 (round 1 REVISE, gating objection from editquality). Phase B3e: the planner prompt is the last unfilled place of DIR-001's seven-place kind lockstep. Since 432, a greenfield finance build carries content_features.<spec_key> at plan time - but build-site-planner had NO rule reading those keys, so the flag sat unread and the site acquired its directory page and homepage section only via the discovery-check round trip, one sweep late and after the first deploy had shipped without them. Migration 433 (applied 2026-08-15) splices a Directory rule after the News listing rule plus RULES entry 18. ROUND-1 DISPOSITION, honest on each: (1) THE GATING OBJECTION IS ANSWERED AT THE ARTEFACT, not argued - editquality asked whether content_features is actually piped into the rendered prompt via input_fields, correctly naming the failure mode where prompt text references unwired data and sits inert. It is wired, and the proof is the rendered prompts themselves: of 66 real build-site-planner/plan_site calls in llm_call_log, 5 contain the literal DATA form 'content_features:map[' and the same 5 contain 'news_feed:map[' (verbatim from the newest, 2026-08-11: 'content_features:map[news_feed:map[reason:... recommended:true separate_page:true ...]]'). The other 61 are sites whose classification spec has no such key at all - which is what makes this measurement disconfirmable rather than a tautology: the count tracks the data, not the template. site_specs IS in plan_site.input_fields and the prompt renders 'Classification: {{.site_specs.specs.classification}}' as a Go map, so every key present in the classification spec appears; content_features is written INTO that same spec by evaluate_directory_features' deep merge. (2) bug_historian's objection was RIGHT to press and produced a real change, migration 441: 433 enumerated every component and page name EXCEPT the listing component, which it asked the model to DERIVE by suffixing - the one derivable name was the one exception, and a paraphrased component name is dropped by validate_site_plan silently. 441 enumerates all six listing names and states the consequence of paraphrasing. The underlying safety claim is also now measured rather than assumed: the names 433 teaches are content_components.FUNCTION values, and function is the canonical resolution target - componentNameResolver.resolve()'s FIRST arm is 'already a valid function -> return unchanged' (v3_site_actions.go:3896-3898). name <> function for all 12 directory rows (name is prose, 'UK Mortgage Lender Directory'), so teaching name would have been exactly the defect the seat feared; teaching function is the safest input, not a lucky one. (3) reuse_agent asked whether the OLDER path becomes a no-op rather than a second creator: it does, by construction - MissingDirectoryPageCheck counts pages of that page_type and returns an empty CheckResult when pageCount>0 (check_directory.go:338-348), and MissingDirectorySectionCheck does the same on a page_components join against the snippet component (lines 251-266). The plan-time path simply satisfies the check's own precondition. (4) debug_historian asked for a snapshot before the jsonb_set: the applied file's FIRST line is SELECT snapshot_agent('build-site-planner', '433...: pre-update') and the guard block refuses if that backup row is absent - a sketch-visibility artefact, now quoted verbatim below. This is the FOURTH round in this lane lost to showing reviewers less than the file contains; it is now a checklist item. (5) guardian's no-SELECT-FOR-UPDATE point is acknowledged unchanged: it matches the platform's existing verify-block idiom and the in-transaction DO/RAISE verify aborts on the drift it describes. (6) guardian asked for blast radius on record: build-site-planner's plan_site output is consumed by the greenfield build pipeline and by recompose_pages redesign runs; both are named below. (7) The prompt-size cost is now measured rather than estimated: real rendered prompts run 40-85KB, so 433's ~2.4KB is roughly 3-6% of a real render, on a step already carrying a 20KB template.

plan.summary: Round 2. Migration 433 (applied): the Directory rule + RULES 18 in build-site-planner's plan_site prompt. Round-1's gating objection (is content_features actually piped into the prompt?) is answered by measurement at the artefact - 5 of 66 real rendered prompts carry the literal data form 'content_features:map[', the other 61 being sites with no such key. Round-1's medium objection about derived component names produced a real change: NEW migration 441 enumerates all six listing component names instead of asking the model to derive one by suffixing, and states that a paraphrased component name is dropped silently.
plan.risks: (1) The rule enumerates the six keys explicitly, so a SEVENTH directory kind must edit this prompt again - that is DIR-001's documented seven-place lockstep, now with the planner-prompt place filled. (2) Prompt cost measured, not estimated: real rendered plan_site prompts are 40-85KB (llm_call_log, n=66), so 433's ~2.4KB is ~3-6% of a render. (3) A planner hallucinating a directory page WITHOUT the flag was already possible; the rule forbids it twice and the publish leg's opt-in gate means such a page ships an empty shell rather than wrong data - unchanged residual, stated for completeness. (4) In-flight planner runs carry their own workflow snapshot; config is live for the next dispatch. (5) The six directory page_type values are unknown to the Go role validator BY DESIGN - verified they pass through untouched (normaliseRole default arm; CanonicalisePage default arm preserves type, name=slug, url=/<slug>.html, the exact shape of the three live pages). (6) ORDERING, load-bearing: 441 edits text inside the block 433 inserted, so while 441 is applied 433's surgical-inverse ROLLBACK cannot match its literal and REFUSES by design - to undo the pair, run 441's ROLLBACK first. Both files' headers say so. (7) Blast radius on record: plan_site's output is consumed by the greenfield build pipeline and by recompose_pages redesign runs; this rule fires for neither unless the site's classification carries a directory key, which no site does today.

edits.rationale: Forward migration, APPLIED and unedited - it is the record of what ran. Round 1 asked for the snapshot call and the guard block; both are quoted verbatim above (the snapshot is the file's first line, and the guard REFUSES if its backup row is absent). Anchors measured unique pre-apply (1|1|0); active rows measured exactly 1; dry run passed all guards with UPDATE 1 before the real apply; read back live after.

edits.sketch:
-- Surgical inverse, NOT restore-from-backup (backup row snapshots the WHOLE
-- config; restoring would clobber later unrelated edits by other sessions).
-- Same exactly-one-active-row guard as forward (the 432 round-1 lesson: a
-- rollback without the guards runs at the worst possible moment):
    IF n <> 1 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION '433 ROLLBACK: build-site-planner does not have exactly one active row (found %) - resolve the ambiguity before editing', n;
    END IF;
    IF (length(p) - length(replace(p, 'Directory rule:', ''))) / length('Directory rule:') <> 1 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION '433 ROLLBACK: Directory rule not present exactly once - 433 is not applied, or the prompt was edited since; inspect before rolling back';
    END IF;
-- Inverse replace((anchor + inserted block) -> anchor) for both insertions; the
-- long literals are byte-identical to the forward file by construction, so a
-- post-433 edit inside the inserted block makes the replace find nothing and the
-- verify block REFUSE (the correct failure). Verify: both blocks gone, both
-- anchors restored to exactly once.

grounded_in: GATING OBJECTION, measured at the artefact 2026-08-16: SELECT over llm_call_log WHERE agent_type='build-site-planner' AND step_name='plan_site' returns 66 rows; 5 carry the literal DATA form 'content_features:map[' and the SAME 5 carry 'news_feed:map['. Verbatim from the newest such render (2026-08-11 10:21:42Z): "content_features:map[news_feed:map[reason:AI field changes rapidly - research, product launches, regulation recommended:true separate_page:true source_types:[rss news_search api_news] ...]]". The other 61 renders are sites whose classification spec carries no content_features key at all - the count tracks the DATA, so it could have come out otherwise. The identical shape is what a directory key renders as.

The wiring path, read rather than assumed: plan_site.config.input_fields = [input_data, site_specs, available_components, available_styles, existing_pages]; the prompt renders 'Classification: {{.site_specs.specs.classification}}' as a Go map (verbatim from a real render: 'Classification: map[category:interactive confidence:0.97 detected_signals:[...] ...]'), so every key present in the classification spec appears in the prompt. evaluate_directory_features deep-merges content_features.<spec_key> INTO that same classification spec (feed_directory_recommendation_action.go:199-236, supersede-then-insert), which is why the flag arrives by the same route the news flag already does.

END-TO-END PRECEDENT for a rule reading a content_features key out of that map dump: the News listing rule (migration 206, same splice point, same shape) has produced 7 live news-index pages across 6 domains - dartsonline.com, fundamentallyai.com, gaswholesalers.com, robot-hands.com, webdesign.co.uk, and relojistas.com's LOCALISED 'noticias-index', which is precisely the behaviour that rule's text asks for. The mechanism is not theoretical on this estate.

bug_historian's landmine, measured: content_components.name <> function for ALL 12 directory rows (name is prose - 'UK Mortgage Lender Directory' - while function is 'mortgage-lender-directory'). The names 433/441 teach are the FUNCTION values. componentNameResolver.resolve()'s first arm is 'if r.validFunctions[raw] { return raw, true }' (v3_site_actions.go:3896-3898), and loadComponentNameResolver populates validFunctions from component_level IN ('section','element') AND is_active AND function <> '' (lines 3862-3867) - all 12 qualify (measured is_active, component_level='section', no requires-backend tag). So a function string resolves verbatim; it is the canonical target, not a lucky match.

Corroboration from the live artefacts: the three deployed directory pages on ai-agent-orchestration.com store sections [hero, <x>-listing, call-to-action] in pages.sections - i.e. FUNCTION values, post-validation. The composition 433 prescribes is the composition that survived this exact pipeline.

Since migration 439 (another lane, landed 2026-08-16 mid-session) validate_plan also carries menu_field='available_components', so the planner's own menu rows are added to the valid set alongside the section/element base - both resolution paths now cover these 12.

reuse_agent's question, answered from the checks' own code: MissingDirectoryPageCheck queries COUNT(*) FROM pages WHERE site_id=$1 AND page_type=$2 and returns an empty CheckResult when pageCount>0 (check_directory.go:338-348); MissingDirectorySectionCheck does the same via a page_components join on the snippet component (lines 251-266). The plan-time path satisfies the older path's precondition, so the older path becomes a no-op rather than a second creator.

debug_historian's snapshot: the applied 433 file's FIRST line is SELECT snapshot_agent('build-site-planner', '433_planner_directory_rule_b3e.sql: pre-update'), and its guard block RAISEs if no backup row with that reason exists. Both are quoted verbatim in edit 1's sketch this round.

directoryCheckProfiles (check_directory.go:72-149) is the single source of the SpecKey -> SnippetComponent/ListingComponent/PageType/PageName mapping both migrations state; PageName = PageType for all six kinds.

page_role_validator.go:249 (normaliseRole default: unknown roles pass through) + page_canonical.go:249-263 (default arm: name=slug, url=/<slug>.html, pageType preserved): the six directory page_type values survive validate_plan unchanged - no -index suffix, no declared parent, no /<slug>/index.html URL, so the section-index flattening rules cannot fire on them.
Prompt-size cost, measured not estimated: real rendered plan_site prompts range 40,897-85,183 bytes (llm_call_log, n=66, 2026-08-09..2026-08-15), so 433's ~2.4KB addition is ~3-6% of a real render.
